headline: LPR held for an 18th month; CGBs give back 0.2–1bp while policy banks rally as tax fears cool
summary: CGBs edged weaker after November's LPR was left unchanged: the CCDC 10-year rose 0.5bp to 1.580% and the 30-year 0.2bp to 2.042%, with the 7-year (+1.1bp) and 2-year (+0.5bp) leading the back-up while 40–50Y still fell 0.3–0.8bp. Over the week the 10-year is still 3.2bp lower and 2s10s sits at a 1-year flat of 34.7bp. Policy banks outperformed: CDB 10-year fell 0.9bp to 1.681%, cutting its spread over CGB 1.4bp to 10.0bp, and CDB 7Y gained 0.4bp, while ADBC and EXIM 10Y lagged CDB with 0.4bp gains.
drivers: The 1-year and 5-year LPRs stayed at 3.00% and 3.50% for an 18th month, as most of Reuters' survey expected, but five of 28 respondents had looked for a cut after the policy-rate anchor shift. CGB futures slipped 0.02–0.08% and cash yields turned higher in the afternoon, with the 10-year up 0.5bp.
Tax fears cool, policy banks rally

Experts quoted by Securities Times said a tax on government bond interest needs a change in tax law and is not feasible near term, with any change likely limited to new issues. That eased the overhang on taxable policy bank bonds: CDB 10Y fell 0.9bp and its spread over CGB narrowed 1.4bp to 10.0bp, CDB 7Y's to 17.7bp.
Equity rout, but bonds stay near their lows

The Shanghai Composite fell 1.23% and ChiNext 3.54%, after the US tech sell-off and 5% drops in Korea and Japan, with over 5,200 stocks down; banks and the SSE 50 rose. Haven buying kept 40–50Y CGBs falling, but with the 10-year at a 1-year low, traders took profit instead of chasing.
Funding steady despite a large drain

The PBOC injected RMB379.5bn of overnight reverse repos at 1.25% against RMB1.07tn maturing, a net drain of RMB688bn, yet overnight Shibor held at 1.261% and DR001 near 1.25%. The 30-year CGB reopening cleared at 2.0337% with a strong 5.93 bid-cover, and the 2-year at 1.2021% (3.27).
data: As expected, but a minority hoped for a cut, so short-end CGBs drifted 0.5bp higher; loan pricing stays sticky.
+RMB39.5bn to RMB2.08tn; sixth monthly rise, largest since May
Steady haven buying supports CGBs over policy banks and helps the strong yuan.
Industrial output 4.8% y/y (f 5.3%, p 5.5%); retail sales 0.4% (f 0.8%, p 1.1%); FAI YTD −8.1% (f −7.0%, p −7.2%); property investment −21.6%
Broad miss with collapsing investment supports lower yields and the case for more fiscal and monetary support.
Smallest annual fall in 11 months but monthly declines persist, so no lift to credit demand yet.
New loans −RMB100bn (f +RMB20bn, p +RMB1.08tn); TSF RMB1.15tn (f 1.42tn, p 3.55tn); M2 7.1% (f 7.2–7.3%, p 7.2%); M1 4.4% (p 3.2%)
Record-low 4.7% loan growth confirms weak private demand and supports lower yields.
Strong external demand trims the growth-scare case for bonds and triggered mild profit-taking.
Soft consumer prices keep the easing bias; the energy-driven PPI squeezes margins and bonds looked through it.
view: Neutral with a mild bullish lean for the next 1–2 weeks, with the 10-year expected in a 1.55–1.61% CCDC range. At 1.580% the 10-year is at the year's low (0th percentile) and the LPR hold shows the PBOC is in no hurry to cut, so I stay out of outright duration until a back-up toward 1.61–1.62%; overnight funding at the 1.25% anchor, fading fund redemptions and weak equities still limit the upside in yields. On the curve I prefer spread to duration: CDB 7Y at 17.7bp over CGB is the cheapest policy bank point, while the CGB belly stays rich and long policy banks are near 1-year tights. Month-end funding strain with DR001 above 1.35%, a formal bond-interest tax plan or a strong November PMI would push the 10-year to 1.62%; a further equity slide or PBOC easing signal would take it toward 1.55%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year rose 0.5bp to 1.233% (9th percentile, average 1.299%) and the 1-year 0.2bp to 1.175% after the LPR hold; the 2-year reopening cleared at 1.2021%. With overnight funding at 1.25%, the 2-year pays little over the anchor, so carry is thin.
buckets.call: Hold; add 2-year CGBs only above 1.27%, or if DR001 settles below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: The belly stays rich: 2s5s10s is −16.1bp (8th percentile, average −8.1bp) with the 5-year unchanged at 1.326%, while the 7-year cheapened 1.1bp to 1.437%. 5s10s is 25.4bp (31st percentile, average 26.7bp), near where Thursday's flattener was closed, so no new edge.
buckets.call: Flat after taking profit at 24.9bp; re-enter the 5s10s flattener at 28bp or wider, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: The 10-year rose 0.5bp to 1.580% but is still 3.2bp lower on the week and at the 0th percentile of its year (average 1.751%); Thursday's long was closed at 1.575%. Against neighbours it is fair (7s10s20s −30.3bp, 42nd percentile), so only the outright level is rich.
buckets.call: Flat; re-buy the 10-year at 1.61–1.62%, target 1.57%, stop 1.65%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: The 30-year rose 0.2bp to 2.042% (2nd percentile, average 2.213%) and 10s30s is 46.1bp (49th percentile, average 46.2bp). The 30-year reopening drew a strong 5.93 bid-cover at 2.0337%, and 30s50s at 9.4bp is a 1-year low, so 50Y remains the richest point.
buckets.call: Neutral; add 30-year CGBs above 2.10% (10s30s ~48bp); poor risk/reward below 2.02%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: The CDB 10-year spread over CGB narrowed 1.4bp to 10.0bp (59th percentile, average 9.6bp) as tax fears cooled, so the 12bp entry was never filled. At 2–5Y policy banks sit at 1-year tights (CDB 2Y 11.4bp, 0th percentile; 5Y 11.4bp, 17th), so value is only at 7–10Y.
buckets.call: Not filled; buy CDB 10Y vs CGB 10Y at 12bp or wider, target 9bp, stop 15bp; avoid 1–5Y policy banks.

buckets.name: Policy banks 5–7Y vs CGB
buckets.why: The CDB 7-year spread over CGB narrowed 1.5bp to 17.7bp (69th percentile, average 15.8bp) and ADBC 7Y is 16.9bp (82nd percentile). Easing tax worries and the end of fund selling are starting to compress the tenor, but it is still the cheapest part of the policy bank curve.
buckets.call: Flat; re-enter CDB 7Y vs CGB 7Y at 21bp or wider, target 17bp, stop 24bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 2.1bp over CDB (62nd percentile, average 1.4bp), 0.5bp more than Thursday as CDB led the rally, a small loss on the ADBC preference. EXIM is 1.5bp (21st percentile, average 2.0bp); at 5Y, ADBC and EXIM sit 3.1bp and 2.4bp over CDB (90th and 95th percentiles).
buckets.call: Hold ADBC 10Y over CDB 10Y for the 2.1bp pickup; switch to CDB below 1bp, cut above 3bp; prefer ADBC/EXIM 5Y over CDB 5Y.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: The CDB 20-year spread over CGB is 10.1bp (55th percentile, average 10.3bp), unchanged on the day. The CDB 30-year spread is 11.0bp, still a 1-year tight (average 12.5bp), so long policy banks offer no value against CGBs.
buckets.call: Flat; re-enter CGB 20Y over CDB 20Y below 7bp; avoid CDB 30Y at an 11bp spread.
